extracted.intended_audience: newspaper reporters and society editors (student and professional journalists writing society/personal news)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reporting and composing society/personal-news items for newspapers, including appropriate form, style, typographical treatment, and decisions about placement and tone for social items such as courtships, engagements, and weddings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain a dedicated society department and editor
rubrics_metrics.description: Interest in social and personal news is so great that practically every newspaper maintains a society department under the direction of a society editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizational/production guideline: assign responsibility to a society editor to manage form, style, and day-to-day coverage of social and personal news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fit form and style to social usage
rubrics_metrics.description: The form and style suitable to such news are partly determined by social usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be sensitive to prevailing social conventions and expectations when choosing how to present society items — tone, emphasis, and phrasing should reflect social norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appropriate typographical style for society columns
rubrics_metrics.description: The typographical style of the society columns often differs somewhat from that of other parts of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select typography and layout (headlines, leads, ornamentation) that suit society copy and distinguish it from general news; adapt visual presentation to audience expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide variety when covering recurring social events
rubrics_metrics.description: Society news taxes the writer's ability to give variety to stories of the same kind of events as they take place day by day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid formulaic repeats — find fresh angles, different emphases, or new human details so routine events don't read the same every time; plan coverage to vary structure and highlight differing hooks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid stock phrases and trite, colorless description
rubrics_metrics.description: In no other kind of news is he more frequently tempted to use stock phrases over and over again... It is possible, however, to give considerable variety to society stories as well as to avoid trite, colorless, description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively eliminate clichés and boilerplate expressions; use vivid, specific detail and original phrasing to keep copy engaging. Treat recurring stylistic temptations as anti-patterns to be corrected in editing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decide placement for unusual social items; develop human-interest without violating taste
rubrics_metrics.description: Unusual courtships, engagements, and weddings may be treated as regular news; in that case the stories of them are not often placed in the society section. Such news not infrequently has humorous and pathetic possibilities that the writer may develop without violating the canons of good taste.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make an editorial decision whether an item belongs in society pages or general news based on its newsworthiness. When developing humorous or poignant angles, do so carefully — exploit human-interest potential but respect standards of decorum and good taste.
